title: ON THE DAY THEY PRESENT THEIR OFFERING

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'or whatever it was they swore falsely about. They must make restitution in full, add a fifth of the value to it and give it all to the owner on the day they present their guilt offering.'" - Lev 6:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two details in this verse deserve attention.

First, a fifth added. The wronged neighbour does not merely get his property back; he receives more than he lost. God's justice does not aim at breaking even. It aims at repair. The victim should end up better than the offence left him.

Second — and this is easy to miss — on the day they present their guilt offering. The repayment and the sacrifice happen on the same day. God does not permit a gap where the person feels forgiven while the neighbour is still waiting.

We are experts at that gap. We settle things with God privately and hope the human side will somehow resolve itself. It rarely does. Someone is still carrying the loss.

Paul urges believers to do what is right in the eyes of everyone, and as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone (Rom 12:17-18). Not just to be at peace with God, but visibly, practically at peace with people.

If you have made things right with God about something, ask yourself the harder question: does the other person know? Has anything actually reached them?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I settled something with God that I have never settled with the person involved?
2. Is there a restitution I have been intending to make "someday"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You care about the person I wronged, not only about my conscience. Help me to act today rather than someday. Amen.
